"""D-013 idempotency keys: reservation + atomic completion via route capture.

The mechanism, exactly as D-013 prescribes, in two phases:

* **Phase 1 (reserve).** ``Idempotent("endpoint")`` reads the ``Idempotency-Key`` header,
  hashes the canonical request body, and calls :func:`reserve`, which opens a SEPARATE
  short-lived session, INSERTs an ``IN_PROGRESS`` row, and COMMITs immediately. Two concurrent
  duplicates therefore collide on the natural composite PK ``(tenant_id, endpoint, key)`` — PG's
  unique index arbitrates, SQLite's single-writer lock serializes. On collision the existing row
  decides the outcome: ``COMPLETED`` + matching hash → REPLAY the stored response verbatim with
  header ``Idempotency-Replayed: true`` and no business logic; ``COMPLETED`` + different hash →
  422 ``idempotency.key_reuse`` (a client bug reusing a key for a different body); ``IN_PROGRESS``
  → 409 ``idempotency.in_progress`` (a concurrent duplicate is still running).

* **Phase 2 (capture).** The dependency YIELDS an :class:`IdempotencyContext` bound to the
  request's BUSINESS session. The handler's last act is ``idem.capture(read_schema)`` — it
  ``model_dump``s the exact schema FastAPI will serialize and STAGES the completion UPDATE
  (status → COMPLETED, response_status, response_body, completed_at) on the business session, so
  the document and the replay record commit ATOMICALLY in one ``run_in_uow`` transaction. The
  cardinal invariant: a replayable response exists iff the document exists.

* **Fail-closed.** On a BUSINESS EXCEPTION, the dependency's teardown deletes the dangling
  IN_PROGRESS reservation (committed in its own session) so the client may retry the same key, and
  re-raises — the app's exception handlers render the proper error envelope. (Atlas commits the
  business work via ``run_in_uow`` INSIDE the handler, so a failed handler has already rolled the
  document AND the staged capture UPDATE back; only the separately-committed reservation needs
  cleanup.) On a FORGOTTEN ``capture()`` (handler returned 2xx but never captured), the teardown
  deletes the dangling reservation and logs a server error; it cannot convert the already-sent 2xx
  to a 500 because the run_in_uow commit precedes teardown — a documented deviation from D-013's
  literal "teardown rolls back", which assumed a deferred session-dependency commit (DECISIONS.md).

Replay short-circuit mechanism (FastAPI-idiomatic): :func:`reserve` raises
:class:`IdempotencyReplay` carrying the stored response. ``IdempotencyReplay`` is an
``AtlasError`` subtype whose dedicated handler in ``app.main`` writes the stored
status+body+header — so a completed-key replay never reaches the handler body and the side
effect cannot run twice. A first-time request instead yields the context normally.
"""

import hashlib
import logging
import uuid
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Annotated, Any

import sqlalchemy as sa
from fastapi import Depends, Header, Request
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

I now have the complete picture. Here is the full research report.

## 1. Backend module layout

`backend/app/modules/procurement/` is split (NOT one file), same pattern as finance's ap_router/ar_router:

```
router.py                  — mounts everything, owns Vendor CRUD + approved-items nested resource
requisition_router.py      — purchase requisitions
rfq_router.py              — RFQs
po_router.py               — purchase orders (+ RFQ→PO convert)
goods_receipt_router.py    — goods receipts
invoice_match_router.py    — 3-way invoice matches + match-tolerance config + reorder-scan
approval_rule_router.py    — value-threshold approval rules
constants.py                — enums, permission keys, doc-type/link-type constants
events.py                    — GoodsReceiptPosted, InvoiceMatched (published to inventory/finance)
handlers.py                  — subscribes to manufacturing/industry events (not relevant to this UI slice)
queries.py                   — cross-module read surface (what finance/sales/reporting import)
models/{vendors,requisitions,rfqs,orders,goods_receipts,invoice_matches,approvals}.py
schemas/{same split}.py
service/{vendors,requisitions,rfqs,orders,conversions,approvals,goods_receipts,goods_receipt_reads,
         invoice_matches,invoice_match_post,invoice_match_reads,reorder,_shared}.py
```

All mounted under one prefix `/api/v1/procurement` via `router.include_router(...)` in `router.py` — no second mount in `main.py`.

## 2. Full endpoint list, grouped by concept

Permission constants (from `constants.py`, all registered via `register_permissions`):
```
procurement.vendor.read / .manage
procurement.requisition.read / .manage / .approve
procurement.rfq.read / .manage                    (no approve — sourcing isn't committing)
procurement.po.read / .manage / .approve
procurement.approval_rule.manage                  (no separate read key)
procurement.goods_receipt.read / .manage / .post
procurement.invoice_match.read / .manage / .post
```

### Vendors (`router.py`) — already known, confirmed
| Method | Path | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/vendors` | `vendor.read` | `Page[VendorRead]`, filters: `status`. Supports conditional GET (ETag/304, status folds into fingerprint) |
| POST | `/vendors` | `vendor.manage` | 201, `VendorRead` |
| GET | `/vendors/{id}` | `vendor.read` | `VendorRead` |
| PATCH | `/vendors/{id}` | `vendor.manage` | `VendorRead` |
| GET | `/vendors/{id}/approved-items` | `vendor.read` | `list[VendorApprovedItemRead]` (not paginated) |
| POST | `/vendors/{id}/approved-items` | `vendor.manage` | 201, `VendorApprovedItemRead` |
| DELETE | `/vendors/{id}/approved-items/{item_id}` | `vendor.manage` | 204 |

No Idempotency-Key on any vendor endpoint (master data, not a P2P document).

### Purchase Requisitions (`requisition_router.py`)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body → Response | Idempotency-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/requisitions` | `requisition.manage` | `RequisitionCreate` → 201 `RequisitionDetail` | yes |
| GET | `/requisitions` | `requisition.read` | `Page[RequisitionRead]`; filters `status`, `requested_by` | no |
| GET | `/requisitions/{id}` | `requisition.read` | `RequisitionDetail` | no |
| PATCH | `/requisitions/{id}` | `requisition.manage` | `RequisitionUpdate` → `RequisitionDetail` (DRAFT only) | no |
| POST | `/requisitions/{id}/submit` | `requisition.manage` | none → `RequisitionDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/requisitions/{id}/decision` | `requisition.approve` | `ApprovalDecisionPayload` → `RequisitionDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/requisitions/{id}/cancel` | `requisition.manage` | none → `RequisitionDetail` | no |
| POST | `/requisitions/{id}/convert-to-rfq` | `requisition.manage` | `RfqFromRequisition` → 201 `RfqDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/requisitions/{id}/convert-to-po` | `requisition.manage` | `PurchaseOrderFromRequisition` → 201 `PurchaseOrderDetail` | yes |

### RFQs (`rfq_router.py`)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body → Response | Idempotency-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/rfqs` | `rfq.manage` | `RfqCreate` → 201 `RfqDetail` | yes |
| GET | `/rfqs` | `rfq.read` | `Page[RfqRead]`; filters `status`, `vendor_id` | no |
| GET | `/rfqs/{id}` | `rfq.read` | `RfqDetail` | no |
| POST | `/rfqs/{id}/send` | `rfq.manage` | none → `RfqDetail` (DRAFT→SENT) | yes |
| POST | `/rfqs/{id}/record-quote` | `rfq.manage` | `RecordQuotePayload` → `RfqDetail` (SENT→QUOTED) | yes |
| POST | `/rfqs/{id}/close` | `rfq.manage` | none → `RfqDetail` | no |

### Purchase Orders (`po_router.py`)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body → Response | Idempotency-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/purchase-orders` | `po.manage` | `PurchaseOrderCreate` → 201 `PurchaseOrderDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/rfqs/{rfq_id}/convert-to-po` | `po.manage` | `PurchaseOrderFromRfq` → 201 `PurchaseOrderDetail` | yes |
| GET | `/purchase-orders` | `po.read` | `Page[PurchaseOrderRead]`; filters `status`, `vendor_id` | no |
| GET | `/purchase-orders/{id}` | `po.read` | `PurchaseOrderDetail` | no |
| POST | `/purchase-orders/{id}/send` | `po.manage` | none → `PurchaseOrderDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/purchase-orders/{id}/decision` | `po.approve` | `ApprovalDecisionPayload` → `PurchaseOrderDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/purchase-orders/{id}/cancel` | `po.manage` | none → `PurchaseOrderDetail` | no |

Note: `convert-to-po` from RFQ lives on the PO router under path `/rfqs/{rfq_id}/convert-to-po`, distinct from the requisition-router's `/requisitions/{id}/convert-to-po`.

### Goods Receipts (`goods_receipt_router.py`)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body → Response | Idempotency-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/goods-receipts` | `goods_receipt.manage` | `GoodsReceiptCreate` → 201 `GoodsReceiptDetail` | yes |
| GET | `/goods-receipts` | `goods_receipt.read` | `Page[GoodsReceiptRead]`; filters `purchase_order_id`, `status` | no |
| GET | `/goods-receipts/{id}` | `goods_receipt.read` | `GoodsReceiptDetail` | no |
| POST | `/goods-receipts/{id}/post` | `goods_receipt.post` | none → `GoodsReceiptDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/goods-receipts/{id}/cancel` | `goods_receipt.manage` | none → `GoodsReceiptDetail` (DRAFT only) | no |

Not a background-job pattern — GR post is synchronous, one transaction (GR + N stock moves + journals + PO update), same style as finance journal posting, not like a batch job with polling.

### Invoice Matches + config (`invoice_match_router.py`)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body → Response | Idempotency-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/invoice-matches` | `invoice_match.manage` | `InvoiceMatchCreate` → 201 `InvoiceMatchDetail` | yes |
| GET | `/invoice-matches` | `invoice_match.read` | `Page[InvoiceMatchRead]`; filters `purchase_order_id`, `status` | no |
| GET | `/invoice-matches/{id}` | `invoice_match.read` | `InvoiceMatchDetail` | no |
| POST | `/invoice-matches/{id}/post` | `invoice_match.post` | none → `InvoiceMatchDetail` | yes |
| POST | `/invoice-matches/{id}/override` | `invoice_match.manage` | none → `InvoiceMatchDetail` (EXCEPTION→MATCHED) | no |
| POST | `/invoice-matches/{id}/cancel` | `invoice_match.manage` | none → `InvoiceMatchDetail` | no |
| GET | `/match-tolerances` | `invoice_match.read` | `MatchToleranceRead \| None` | no |
| PUT | `/match-tolerances` | `invoice_match.manage` | `MatchToleranceUpsert` → `MatchToleranceRead` | no |
| POST | `/reorder-scan` | `requisition.manage` (not invoice_match!) | none → `RequisitionDetail \| None` (201 if created, 200 null if nothing to reorder) | yes |

### Approval Rules (`approval_rule_router.py`)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body → Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/approval-rules` | `approval_rule.manage` | `ApprovalRuleCreate` → 201 `ApprovalRuleRead` |
| GET | `/approval-rules` | `approval_rule.manage` | `Page[ApprovalRuleRead]`; filters `document_type`, `is_active` |
| GET | `/approval-rules/{id}` | `approval_rule.manage` | `ApprovalRuleRead` |
| PATCH | `/approval-rules/{id}` | `approval_rule.manage` | `ApprovalRuleUpdate` → `ApprovalRuleRead` |

No document-creating endpoints here (config, not a document), no idempotency.

### Cross-cutting: Document flow viewer (core, not procurement)
`GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/chain` → `DocChainResponse { nodes: DocChainNode[], edges: DocChainEdge[] }`. Every procurement document header exposes `document_id` — use this generic core endpoint to render the requisition→RFQ→PO→GR→match chain (same viewer you presumably already wired for finance/inventory docflow).

## 3. Full schema field-by-field

### Vendors (`schemas/vendors.py`)
```ts
VendorCreate:  { vendor_code: string; name: string; default_currency_code: string(3);
  status?: VendorStatus="ACTIVE"; payment_terms_days?: number=30; tax_reference?: string|null;
  email?; phone?; address?; notes?: string|null }
VendorUpdate:  same but all optional, NO vendor_code (immutable)
VendorRead:    { id, vendor_code, name, status: VendorStatus, default_currency_code,
  payment_terms_days: number, tax_reference, email, phone, address, notes,
  created_at, updated_at }
VendorFilter:  { status?: VendorStatus }
VendorApprovedItemCreate: { item_id: uuid; vendor_item_code?: string|null; is_active?: boolean=true }
VendorApprovedItemRead:   { id, vendor_id, item_id, vendor_item_code, is_active, created_at }
```
`VendorStatus = "ACTIVE" | "BLOCKED" | "INACTIVE"` — **your existing stub's `VendorStatus` type is wrong**: it only has `"ACTIVE" | "INACTIVE"`, missing `BLOCKED`, and `VendorRead` in the stub lacks `updated_at`. Fix both when replacing the stub.

### Requisitions (`schemas/requisitions.py`)
```ts
RequisitionLineCreate: { item_id: uuid; description?: string|null; quantity: Decimal;
  uom_id: uuid; estimated_unit_cost?: Decimal|null; currency_code: string(3) }
RequisitionCreate: { requested_by?: uuid|null; needed_by_date?: date|null; notes?: string|null;
  lines: RequisitionLineCreate[] }   // >=1 line required
RequisitionUpdate: { requested_by?; needed_by_date?; notes?; lines?: RequisitionLineCreate[]|null }
  // DRAFT only; supplying lines replaces them wholesale
RequisitionLineRead: { id, line_number: number, item_id, description, quantity: Decimal,
  uom_id, estimated_unit_cost: Decimal|null, currency_code }
RequisitionRead: { id, requisition_number: string, status: RequisitionStatus,
  requested_by: uuid|null, needed_by_date: date|null, notes, document_id: uuid,
  created_at, updated_at }
RequisitionDetail: RequisitionRead & { lines: RequisitionLineRead[] }
RequisitionFilter: { status?: RequisitionStatus; requested_by?: uuid }
ApprovalDecisionPayload: { decision: "APPROVED"|"REJECTED"; comment?: string|null }
```
`RequisitionStatus = DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CONVERTED | CANCELLED`

### RFQs (`schemas/rfqs.py`)
```ts
RfqLineCreate: { item_id, description?, quantity: Decimal, uom_id }   // no price at create
RfqCreate: { vendor_id: uuid; currency_code: string(3); valid_until?: date|null; notes?;
  lines: RfqLineCreate[] }
RfqFromRequisition: { vendor_id: uuid; currency_code?: string|null; valid_until?; notes? }
RfqLineQuote: { line_id: uuid; quoted_unit_cost: Decimal }
RecordQuotePayload: { quotes: RfqLineQuote[] }
RfqLineRead: { id, line_number, item_id, description, quantity, uom_id, quoted_unit_cost: Decimal|null }
RfqRead: { id, rfq_number, status: RfqStatus, vendor_id, currency_code, valid_until: date|null,
  source_requisition_id: uuid|null, notes, document_id, created_at, updated_at }
RfqDetail: RfqRead & { lines: RfqLineRead[] }
RfqFilter: { status?: RfqStatus; vendor_id?: uuid }
```
`RfqStatus = DRAFT | SENT | QUOTED | CLOSED | CANCELLED`

### Purchase Orders (`schemas/orders.py`)
```ts
PurchaseOrderLineCreate: { item_id, description?, quantity: Decimal, uom_id, unit_cost: Decimal,
  tax_code_id?: uuid|null }
PurchaseOrderCreate: { vendor_id: uuid; currency_code?: string|null; order_date?: date|null;
  expected_date?: date|null; notes?; lines: PurchaseOrderLineCreate[] }
PurchaseOrderFromRequisition: { vendor_id: uuid; order_date?; expected_date?; notes? }
PurchaseOrderFromRfq: { order_date?; expected_date?; notes? }   // vendor comes from the RFQ
PurchaseOrderLineRead: { id, line_number, item_id, description, quantity, uom_id,
  unit_cost: Decimal, line_amount: Decimal, received_quantity: Decimal, tax_code_id: uuid|null }
  // NOTE: billed_quantity exists on the ORM model but is NOT in PurchaseOrderLineRead —
  // it's only surfaced via InvoiceMatchLineRead's po_unit_cost/variances; frontend cannot read
  // a PO line's billed_quantity directly from the PO detail endpoint.
PurchaseOrderRead: { id, po_number, status: PurchaseOrderStatus, vendor_id, currency_code,
  order_date: date, expected_date: date|null, payment_terms_days: number,
  total_amount: Decimal, notes, approved_by: uuid|null, approved_at: string|null,
  source_requisition_id: uuid|null, source_rfq_id: uuid|null, document_id, created_at, updated_at }
PurchaseOrderDetail: PurchaseOrderRead & { lines: PurchaseOrderLineRead[] }
PurchaseOrderFilter: { status?: PurchaseOrderStatus; vendor_id?: uuid }
```
`PurchaseOrderStatus = DRAFT | PENDING_APPROVAL | APPROVED | REJECTED | SENT | PARTIALLY_RECEIVED | RECEIVED | CLOSED | CANCELLED`

### Goods Receipts (`schemas/goods_receipts.py`)
```ts
GoodsReceiptLineCreate: { purchase_order_line_id: uuid; bin_id: uuid; received_quantity: Decimal;
  lot_code?: string|null; serial_code?: string|null; requires_inspection?: boolean|null }
  // item_id/unit_cost are NOT client-settable — snapshotted server-side from the PO line
GoodsReceiptCreate: { purchase_order_id: uuid; warehouse_id: uuid; receipt_date?: date|null;
  notes?; lines: GoodsReceiptLineCreate[] }
GoodsReceiptLineRead: { id, line_number, purchase_order_line_id, item_id, bin_id,
  received_quantity: Decimal, unit_cost: Decimal, lot_code, serial_code,
  requires_inspection: boolean }
GoodsReceiptRead: { id, gr_number, status: GoodsReceiptStatus, purchase_order_id, vendor_id,
  warehouse_id, receipt_date: date, notes, posted_at: string|null, document_id,
  created_at, updated_at }
GoodsReceiptDetail: GoodsReceiptRead & { lines: GoodsReceiptLineRead[] }
GoodsReceiptFilter: { purchase_order_id?: uuid; status?: GoodsReceiptStatus;
  date_from?: date; date_to?: date }
```
`GoodsReceiptStatus = DRAFT | POSTED | CANCELLED`

### Invoice Matches (`schemas/invoice_matches.py`)
```ts
InvoiceMatchLineCreate: { purchase_order_line_id: uuid; goods_receipt_line_id?: uuid|null;
  matched_quantity: Decimal; unit_price: Decimal }
InvoiceMatchCreate: { purchase_order_id: uuid; vendor_invoice_ref?: string|null;
  invoice_date?: date|null; tax_code_id?: uuid|null; notes?; lines: InvoiceMatchLineCreate[] }
  // total_amount is server-computed, never accepted from client
InvoiceMatchLineRead: { id, line_number, purchase_order_line_id, goods_receipt_line_id: uuid|null,
  item_id, matched_quantity: Decimal, unit_price: Decimal, po_unit_cost: Decimal,
  price_variance: Decimal, quantity_variance: Decimal, line_amount: Decimal,
  within_tolerance: boolean }
InvoiceMatchRead: { id, match_number, status: MatchStatus, purchase_order_id, vendor_id,
  vendor_invoice_ref, invoice_date: date, currency_code, total_amount: Decimal,
  tax_code_id: uuid|null, notes, document_id, posted_at: string|null, created_at, updated_at }
InvoiceMatchDetail: InvoiceMatchRead & { lines: InvoiceMatchLineRead[] }
InvoiceMatchFilter: { purchase_order_id?: uuid; status?: MatchStatus }
MatchToleranceUpsert: { price_tolerance_percent?: Decimal=0; quantity_tolerance_percent?: Decimal=0 }
MatchToleranceRead: { id, price_tolerance_percent: Decimal, quantity_tolerance_percent: Decimal,
  created_at, updated_at }
```
`MatchStatus = DRAFT | MATCHED | EXCEPTION | POSTED | CANCELLED`

### Approval Rules (`schemas/approvals.py`)
```ts
ApprovalRuleCreate: { document_type: "REQUISITION"|"PURCHASE_ORDER"; threshold_amount: Decimal(>=0);
  currency_code: string(3); is_active?: boolean=true; description?: string|null }
ApprovalRuleUpdate: { threshold_amount?; currency_code?; is_active?; description? }  // no document_type (immutable key)
ApprovalRuleRead: { id, document_type, threshold_amount: Decimal, currency_code, is_active,
  description, created_at, updated_at }
ApprovalRuleFilter: { document_type?; is_active?: boolean }
```

All `Decimal` fields serialize as JSON strings (D-015 exact-decimal convention — matches finance's `MoneyType`/`QuantityType` pattern you already handle in the finance frontend).

## 4. Document-flow chain, field linkage, and lifecycle transitions

```
Requisition (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED/REJECTED, →CONVERTED, →CANCELLED)
  │  convert-to-rfq (requisition must be APPROVED) ─┐
  │  convert-to-po  (requisition must be APPROVED) ─┼─→ PurchaseOrder.source_requisition_id
  ▼                                                  │
RFQ (DRAFT→SENT→QUOTED→CLOSED, →CANCELLED)          │
  │  convert-to-po (RFQ must be QUOTED) ─────────────┘
  ▼                                       PurchaseOrder.source_rfq_id
PurchaseOrder
  DRAFT → send → {PENDING_APPROVAL (needs po.approve decision) | APPROVED} → SENT
  → (GR posts) → PARTIALLY_RECEIVED | RECEIVED
  → (Match posts, fully received+billed) → CLOSED
  REJECTED / CANCELLED are terminal side-branches
  ▼
GoodsReceipt (DRAFT→POSTED, →CANCELLED; POSTED terminal)
  created against SENT/APPROVED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED PO; raises PO line received_quantity
  ▼
InvoiceMatch (DRAFT→MATCHED|EXCEPTION→POSTED, →CANCELLED; POSTED terminal, EXCEPTION→override→MATCHED)
  created against PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED PO (needs received-not-billed qty)
  → post publishes InvoiceMatched → FINANCE creates+posts the AP vendor bill (its own module)
```

Key quantity fields on `PurchaseOrderLine` (server-maintained, only `received_quantity` is exposed in `PurchaseOrderLineRead`; `billed_quantity` exists in the ORM but is not in that read schema):
- `quantity` (ordered), `received_quantity` (raised by GR post), `billed_quantity` (raised by match post; NOT exposed on PO line read — only inferable via InvoiceMatchLineRead's own quantity fields).
- Open-to-receive = `quantity - received_quantity`; open-to-bill = `received_quantity - billed_quantity`.

Docflow link types (edge = predecessor→successor, `link_type` string):
- `sourced_by` — requisition → RFQ
- `ordered_by` — RFQ→PO and requisition→PO (straight order)
- `received_by` — PO → GR
- `moved_by` — GR → inventory stock move (written by inventory's handler, not procurement)
- `matched_by` — PO → match, and each distinct GR feeding the match → match
- `billed_by` — match → finance vendor bill (written by finance's handler)

**The vendor bill itself is NOT created by any procurement endpoint.** `POST /invoice-matches/{id}/post` publishes the `InvoiceMatched` domain event; finance's handler creates+posts the AP vendor bill in the same transaction. The frontend never calls a "create bill" endpoint from procurement — after posting a match, the resulting bill is visible only through finance's existing `VendorBillListPage`/`VendorBillDetailPage` (already built), reachable by following the `document_id` → docflow chain (`match.document_id`'s successor edge, `billed_by`) or by looking up the bill under finance AP filtered by vendor/date. There is no procurement schema field carrying the bill's id (deliberately — D-042: "no vendor_bill_id FK").

## 5. Approval workflows (exact status transitions)

Both requisitions and POs use the same data-driven value-threshold rule (`ApprovalRule`, one per tenant per `document_type` ∈ {REQUISITION, PURCHASE_ORDER}):

- **Requisition**: `POST /requisitions/{id}/submit` — DRAFT only. Computes `Σ qty × estimated_unit_cost` (lines with no estimate contribute 0). If a rule is active for REQUISITION, its `currency_code` matches the requisition-lines' currency, and total ≥ `threshold_amount` → status becomes `SUBMITTED` (needs a separate `POST /requisitions/{id}/decision` by someone with `requisition.approve`). Otherwise auto-advances straight to `APPROVED`. `decision` payload: `{decision: APPROVED|REJECTED, comment?}`; only a SUBMITTED requisition can be decided.
- **PO**: `POST /purchase-orders/{id}/send` — from DRAFT: same threshold logic on `total_amount`/`currency_code`; ≥ threshold → `PENDING_APPROVAL` (needs `PO_APPROVE` via `/purchase-orders/{id}/decision`, records `approved_by`+`approved_at`); below → auto `SENT` directly (skips APPROVED, sets `approved_at`). From `APPROVED` status, send just flips to `SENT`. Any other status → 409 `po_not_sendable`.
- No active rule or currency mismatch ⇒ **no gate at all** (auto-approves) — this matters for empty-state UI: a fresh tenant with no `ApprovalRule` rows will never show a pending-approval queue.
- Approval rule currency must exactly match the document's currency or the rule is silently skipped (documented as "no applicable rule", not an error).

## 6. Business semantics for a correct frontend

**Over-receipt cap (goods receipts).** Enforced in `service/goods_receipts.py::_validate_receipt_line`: `received_quantity` per line capped at `PO_line.quantity - PO_line.received_quantity` (open quantity). Exceeding it → 422 `procurement.over_receipt` with `{purchase_order_line_id, open_quantity, received_quantity}` in `details`. The GR-create form must compute/display each candidate PO line's open quantity and validate client-side before submit, but must handle the 422 regardless.

**Over-billing cap (3-way match, the analogue of your "issue #75" over-delivery cap in sales).** This exact cap lives in procurement's `service/invoice_matches.py::_validate_match_line`: `matched_quantity` capped at `PO_line.received_quantity - PO_line.billed_quantity` (received-not-yet-billed). Exceeding → 422 `procurement.over_billing`. This is procurement's own post-time cap, parallel in spirit to whatever sales/#75 does for deliveries — it is NOT shared code with sales; it's a separate enforcement in this module.

**3-way match tolerance / EXCEPTION logic (the "issue #74" quantity-variance fix), confirmed in code with an explicit `#74` comment in `_validate_match_line`:**
- Price variance % = `abs(unit_price - po_unit_cost) / po_unit_cost * 100` (or 100% if po_unit_cost is 0 and price nonzero, 0% if both zero).
- Quantity variance is **not** simply invoiced-vs-received. Expected quantity = the referenced GR line's `received_quantity` if `goods_receipt_line_id` is supplied, else the PO line's open-to-bill quantity. `quantity_variance = max(0, matched_quantity - expected_quantity)` — **billing LESS than expected (a normal partial invoice) is never a variance; only billing MORE than the specific receipt it's tied to counts.** This is the #74 fix: without a GR-line reference or with partial invoicing, a naive comparison would have falsely flagged EXCEPTION on ordinary partial invoices.
- A line is `within_tolerance` iff both price% ≤ `price_tolerance_percent` AND qty% ≤ `quantity_tolerance_percent` (from `MatchTolerance`, default 0/0 = strict — any deviation is exception by default until a tenant configures tolerances via `PUT /match-tolerances`).
- Match header status = `MATCHED` if every line within tolerance, else `EXCEPTION`. `EXCEPTION` blocks `POST /invoice-matches/{id}/post` (409 `match_in_exception`) until `POST /invoice-matches/{id}/override` (requires `invoice_match.manage`, not a separate key) moves it to `MATCHED`.
- Frontend implication: the match line editor should let the user optionally pick a specific `goods_receipt_line_id` per match line (fetched via `GET /goods-receipts?purchase_order_id=...`) rather than leaving it null, since that changes whether a partial-invoice quantity is flagged.

**Receiving triggers inventory stock moves automatically — no separate frontend call.** `POST /goods-receipts/{id}/post` publishes `GoodsReceiptPosted`; inventory's handler creates the stock RECEIPT moves + finance posts the GR/IR journal, all in the same transaction as the GR post. The frontend calls only the one `post` endpoint; there is no "create stock move" step to build. Same pattern for `POST /invoice-matches/{id}/post` → `InvoiceMatched` → finance creates+posts the AP bill automatically.

**No background-job/polling pattern anywhere in procurement.** Every posting action (GR post, match post, PO send, requisition submit) is synchronous, single-request, single-transaction — unlike some finance/inventory bulk operations. The reorder-scan is also inline/synchronous (documented `ponytail`-style: "a per-tenant volume that outgrows the sync budget would move it behind the job runner — documented, not built for v1").

**Idempotency-Key convention** (already used in your finance/inventory work): every document-creating/converting/posting/deciding/sending/submitting endpoint requires `Idempotency-Key` header via `Idempotent("procurement.<op>")`. Read/list/cancel/close/override endpoints do not require it. Your `apiClient.ts` already supports `options.idempotencyKey` → header, with `crypto.randomUUID()` default generator — reuse that helper as-is.

**Vendor status gating.** A PO cannot be created against a BLOCKED or INACTIVE vendor (`require_active_vendor`); RFQ create also requires an ACTIVE vendor. Vendor status transitions are unrestricted (any state ↔ any state) — no terminal vendor state.

**Approved-items enforcement.** Every PO line's item must be an active `VendorApprovedItem` for that vendor (`require_item_approved_for_vendor`), else 422 `procurement.item_not_approved`. The PO line-item picker should be scoped to `GET /vendors/{vendor_id}/approved-items` once a vendor is chosen, not a raw inventory item picker.

**Snapshot/immutable fields to render as read-only, not editable:** GR line's `item_id`/`unit_cost` (snapshotted from PO line, not client-settable in `GoodsReceiptLineCreate`); PO's `payment_terms_days`/`currency_code` (snapshot from vendor at create, immutable after); match line's `po_unit_cost` (snapshot, server-computed).
